Surah Quraysh: its purpose is to indicate the opposite of what Surat al-Fil indicated, namely that the destruction of the stubborn deniers and opponents is for the reform of the near, worshipping servants. This is a great glad tiding specifically for Quraysh, by showing their nobility in both abodes. Its name, Quraysh, clearly indicates this. The expression "Quraysh" rather than "your people" or "al-Hums" or the like indicates that they dominate all people by strength, as the name signifies, and also by a lack of strength, as shown by what He did for their sake in the story of the Elephant.

*"In the name of Allah"*, the One possessing the glorifications and praise, so all perfection belongs to Him; *"the Most Gracious"*, the Possessor of general blessings in bringing into existence and in clarifying, so He is the Possessor of bounties; *"the Most Merciful"*, the Possessor of vengeance through distancing and of singling out whom He wills for felicity through bringing near and exalting.

* *

Since what He, glorified is He, did, by preventing this great army, whose strength includes obedience of the greatest land animal that Allah created, as far as we know, from entering the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), which is the manifestation of His power and the place of His dazzling greatness and might, and which recalls His friend (Khalil, Abraham), upon whom be prayers and peace, and his fulfilment of the great friendship with Him, it was a great, evident and immediate honour for Quraysh, a protection for them from having their homes plundered and their offspring taken captive, because they are the sons of His friend, the servants of His House, the inhabitants of His Sanctuary, those strengthened by it and devoted to Him. It also protected them from the ruin of the homeland of their might, the place of their security, livelihood and refuge. He, glorified and exalted is He, reminded them of the deferred blessing it contained, as a second honour, by considering the outcome. So He said, indicating that whoever exalts himself against Him, He breaks, and whoever humbles himself to Him and serves Him, He honours and magnifies: ﴿For the accustoming of Quraysh﴾, i.e., for this matter and no other did We do that. It is their establishment of the accustoming (ilaf), which is their familiarity with their land, from which arises their tranquillity and the awe that people have for them. This necessarily entails their being accustomed first within themselves. When they had familiarity with their Sanctuary, through the might and capacity they obtained by it, with what He defended them in, along with His removing the calamities far from them, and when they had familiarity among themselves, so that some of them became accustomed to others, their affair grew strong, and so they accustomed others, i.e., they made others accustomed to what they were accustomed to, that is, they set it as a custom for them and commanded them with it. Or the lam may be connected to the verb of worship, as indicated by ﴿so let them worship﴾ [Quraysh: 3], i.e., so that they worship Us, because of what We established of their familiarity and accustoming. Under both interpretations, the accustoming is the cause of worship, or of what necessitates gratitude through worship. In this there is an indication of the complete power of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and that when He wills something He facilitates its cause, because all the arrangement belongs to Him. He lowers whom He wills, even if he is mighty, and raises whom He wills, even if he is humbled, so that the belief in this produces love of Him, devotion to His worship, and reliance on Him for every benefit and protection.

Quraysh are the descendants of al-Nadr ibn Kinana, and their name and the name of their tribe is derived from *al-qirsh* (the gathering and earning of livelihood) and *al-tagarrush*, which is earning and gathering. It is said: so-and-so *yaqrush* for his dependants and *yaqtarish*, i.e., earns. Al-Baghawi said: Abu Raydhana said: Mu'awiya asked Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Why were they named by this?" He said: "After a creature in the sea which is the greatest of its animals, called *al-qirsh*. It does not pass anything, lean or fat, without eating it. It eats and is not eaten, and it rises and is not risen over." He said: "Do the Arabs know that in their poetry?" He said: "Yes," and he recited for al-Jumahi:

Quraysh are those who dwell in the sea by them,
Quraysh were named Quraysh.

They rule by height in the depth of the sea over
all the armies, armies.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "It is a great creature that plays with ships and cannot be subdued except by fire, and the diminutive form is for magnification." End of quote. It was said: they were named this because they gathered at the Sanctuary after their dispersal, since *al-qirsh*, as already mentioned, is gathering, and their gathering place was far off. *Al-qirsh* also means strong. It was said it is from *taqarrasha al-rajul*, when a man kept himself away from base affairs, and *taqarashat al-rimah fi'l-harb*, when the spears entered into one another in battle. The whole root is for strength and intermixing. The use of this name is for their praise. As Allah, glorified and exalted is He, caused their praise to flow on tongues, He made them a locus of praise. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah chose Kinana from the sons of Isma'il, chose Quraysh from Kinana, chose Banu Hashim from Quraysh, and chose me from Banu Hashim." He (ﷺ) also said: "The leaders are from Quraysh." The scholars said: this is because pure lineage leads to good character, good character leads to purity of heart, purity of heart aids in grasping the sciences, and by grasping the sciences one attains the lofty ranks in [this world and] the Hereafter. Here the name is declined in the sense of "living", so that the name by its root indicates gathering, and by its declension indicates life, as an indication of the perfection of their life outwardly and inwardly. Sibawayh said regarding Ma'add, Quraysh and Thaqif: "Declining these tribes is more common, but if you make them names of tribes, i.e., not declined, that is permissible and good." What indicates that the lam is connected to a verb that the Elephant indicates is that the two surahs in the codex of Ubayy, may Allah be pleased with him, are a single surah without separation. Also, 'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Shayba narrated from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, led us in the maghrib prayer and recited in the first rak'a al-Tin and al-Zaytun, and in the second: *Alam tara kayfa* and *li-ilaf Quraysh*."

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: "There is an obscurity in their connection, i.e., that He, glorified and exalted is He, did that to the people of the Elephant and prevented them from His House and Sanctuary in order to unite the shaml (cohesion) of Quraysh, who are the inhabitants of the Sanctuary and the dwellers of the Sacred House of Allah, and to bring them together by these two journeys, so that they would settle in Makka and its precincts would be secure." End of quote.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 106, verse 2:

When He gave the reason by ﴿the familiarity of the Quraysh﴾, and "ilaf" (familiarity, accustoming) is both intransitive and transitive, one says: "I became familiar with (ālaftu) the place, I become familiar with it (ūlifuhu) with familiarity (ilāfan), so I am familiarized (mu'allaf)." And "I made so-and-so familiar (ālaftu) with this thing," meaning, "you made him one who is accustomed to it (ālif) to it." When bringing a thing is open to two readings, and then one of them is replaced by it, this is more grand for its matter and higher for its affair. The replacement here is His words ﴿their familiarity﴾, meaning "Our making them familiar," ﴿the caravan of winter﴾, which they used to set out on in his time toward Yemen, because it is a hot land from which they obtain the merchandise of the south; ﴿and summer﴾, which they used to set out on toward Syria in his time, because it is a cold land from which they obtain the benefits of the north. They were secure from the rest of the Arabs because of their honour in the sacred, esteemed, and venerated Sanctuary (p-٢٦٤) of God's House, while people were being snatched away from around them. So God Most High did to the People of the Elephant what He did, so that the Arabs would increase in awe and reverence of them and would increase in honouring them, seeing God Most High's honouring of them. Thus they had the utmost ability to carry on their journeys. "Ar-rihlah" with a kasra is the manner of departing, and it was read with a damma, which is the direction toward which one departs. They were excused for this, because their land had no crops [and no livestock -]. So when they travelled through the land they would say: "We are the inhabitants of God's Sanctuary and the custodians of His House," so no one would attack them with harm. Had it not been for the two journeys, they would have had no settlement in Mecca, and had it not been for the security by the protection of the House, they would not have been able to conduct their affairs. The first to establish the journey for them was Hashim ibn Abd Manaf. They used to divide their profit between the rich and the poor, until their poor were like their rich. On this the poet says:

Say to the one who seeks generosity and liberality: "Why did you not pass by the family of Abd Manaf?"

Those who give provision, though there is none who gives provision, and those who say "Come, for hospitality,"

And those who mix their poor with their rich, until their poor is like the one who withholds (from need),

Those who say, with every true promise, and those who depart on the journey of familiarity,

'Amr al-'Ula crushed the bread (tharid) for his people, while the men of Mecca were in drought, lean and wasted,

(p-٢٦٥) Two journeys he established for himself and his people: the journey of winter and the journey of summer.

Hashim was followed in this by his brothers. Hashim would make the familiarity to Syria, Abd Shams to Abyssinia, al-Muttalib to Yemen, and Nawfal to Persia. The merchants of Quraysh would travel to these regions under the protection ("hibal," meaning their covenants) of these brothers, which they had obtained for them as security from the king of each region [of these regions -]. He used the word "rihlah" in the singular, though the context calls for the dual, to encompass every journey, as is the usage of verbal nouns and generic nouns. It is an indication [for them -] of good tidings: that they would soon be able to journey to whatever land they wished, because security was extended to them, and through them to all the earth, by the good that God, glorified and exalted, spread in the hearts of His servants throughout the earth, through this Noble Prophet, who is the most noble, greatest, most majestic, and most generous of them.

When al-Biqa'i's commentary (Nazm al-Durar) reaches this point, the argument is as follows. Since this arrangement from God for them (the people of Quraysh) was sufficient to remove their outward worries of poverty and their inward worries of fear, and since thanking the bestower of favour is obligatory, then when He bestows a favour upon someone that leaves the one bestowed upon free to give thanks, the obligation of thanks upon him becomes greater. Consequent upon His bestowing this favour upon them, He said: ﴿So let them worship﴾, that is, Quraysh, as an obligation, giving thanks for this particular blessing, if they do not give thanks for all His countless blessings, because they claim (p-266) that they are the most thankful of people for kindness and the furthest of people from ingratitude. ﴿The Lord of this House﴾, that is, the One who brought it into being and who is generous to its people by nurturing them through it, by guarding it from every tyrant, by making it honoured on account of its sanctity against every transgressor, and by humbling the tyrants before it, so that His kindness to them and His compassion towards them may be complete, through the perfecting of their honour for them in this world and the next. He made their continued worship of Him linked to the honour of the Hereafter, so that the blessing is complete and the mercy is perfected. What is meant by "this House" is the Ka'bah. He expressed it with a demonstrative pronoun to magnify it, as an indication that what preceded in the previous surah of defending them is well known, that it was by its cause, and so it needs no explicit statement; and that this made it present in every mind, witnessed by every addressee. In this allusion there is a magnification that an explicit statement does not have. Then He described Himself, the Most Holy, with what is the fruit of the two journeys and a manifestation of the increase in the House's nobility, so He, exalted is He, said:

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 106, verse 4:**

﴿Who has fed them﴾, that is, Quraysh, by bringing provisions to Makkah on the two journeys, safe from being attacked, and by destroying those who intended to ruin the House, the one through which their order subsists. It was feeding that began ﴿after hunger﴾, that is, a great hunger, in which other Arabs were, or they themselves had been before that, because their land was prepared for it, since it has no cultivation. So they were exposed to the poverty that gives rise to hunger. He alone sufficed them for that, and no one shared with Him in providing for them. Therefore it is not gratitude to associate others with Him in worship, nor is it righteousness toward their father Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who prayed for their provision and most strictly forbade the worship of idols. He did not say "He satisfied them" [i.e. the text does not say "He satiated them"], because not all of them used to be satisfied, and because whoever among them was satisfied sought more than what he had.

«The belly of the son of Adam is filled by nothing but dirt.»

Having mentioned the cause of the establishment of their outward life, he mentioned the cause of the establishment of their life through the inward blessing, saying: ﴿And has made them safe﴾, that is, singling them out, ﴿from fear﴾, that is, a very severe fear of the People of the Elephant, and of what would befall them from those around them by way of being snatched away, through killing, plunder and raids; and (they were made safe) from leprosy through the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and from plague and the Dajjal through the protection of the Prophet (ﷺ). From this came the completion, through what He singled them out with of the ilaf (the winter and summer journeys), so it is known that its last part is the cause of its first part. It is also possible that their habit of the land occurred first, and Allah protected them by what was mentioned, so that this was caused by the ilaf; thus the first part is the cause of the last part. Then the two extremes met, and the two seas that feed from each other joined. Just as the end of each surah meets its beginning, so the end of the Mighty Qur'an met its beginning in relation to nine surahs, of which this is the first, when you count from the end to it. Its essential content is the favour upon Quraysh by aiding them in trade, as an ilaf for them through the journey in it and travelling in the land because of it, and by singling them out with the command to worship the One who favoured them with the Sacred House and brought them provision and security through it. Among the greatest aims of al-Tawbah (Repentance, also called Bara'ah), which is opposed to this surah by being the ninth of the first (group), is the disavowal of every apostate, and that doing this is a cause of harmony after what was thought to be a cause of division. It also mentions the virtues of the House and who is fit to serve it, and the attainment of its security and favour, and the good news of wealth in a way greater than obtaining it through trade, and more radiant, more abundant, more glorious and more splendid, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they testify against themselves [of disbelief]﴾ [al-Tawbah: 17], and the verses that follow it, and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾ [al-Tawbah: 28]. From this it is known with clear knowledge that He, glorified is He, began to respond to the ending (maqta') of the surah with the beginning (matla') of Surat Quraysh, the people whom Allah honoured by sending down the Qur'an in their tongue and sending the Prophet (ﷺ) to them, just as He honoured them by building the House for their sake, and by magnifying their wealth and their security. Among the greatest correspondences in this is that the beginning of the surah with which He began responding to the ending with the beginning is very similar to the surah corresponding to it, so much so that in each of the two, together with the one before it, it is like a single surah: Bara'ah with al-Anfal is likewise, to the point that ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) said that the Prophet (ﷺ) died without clarifying its matter, so it was not established for him that it was independent of it. For this reason he did not write the line of Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim between them. But this surah, which is at the end, is certain to be independent, even though it is reported that in the Mushaf of Ubayy (may Allah be pleased with him) the two were one surah, and the recitation of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) joined them in a manner that indicates this, as has passed, as a hint that the latter would be clearer than the former. Among the most remarkable things is that the two surahs before the two corresponding surahs are contrasted in their matters: the first, which is at the end, is al-Fil, in which Allah honoured Quraysh by destroying the [people of the] Elephant. The first, which is at the beginning, is al-Anfal, in which Allah honoured them by giving victory to the People of the Qur'an over them, by destroying their tyrants. So that was a cause of breaking their power and the fall of their arrogance, which led to their happiness. He knew that Bara'ah and the others were revealed only to honour them, because they are the ones intended in essence and as the primary purpose of sending, and the people are followers of them, just as all the Messengers are followers of the Messenger, the Conqueror, the Seal, whom they were honoured to be sent to (ﷺ). The number nine indicates that Quraysh are fit to connect with the ascent of secrets in the celestial realm to the ninth sphere, which is the Throne, the reverse of the Law. So they ascend with the secrets of the Law, the greatest of which is prayer, from below to above, from both extremes together, just as blessings descend upon them from both sides. If you add the first nine to the others, they become eighteen, and so they indicate the units of the prayers with the witr added to them, and the complete manifestation of the religion over most of the regions of the earth, as occurred in the year twenty-eight, which is the eighteenth year after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), during the caliphate of ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him). In it the kingdom of Kisra was torn apart and greatly weakened, and likewise the kingdom of the Romans, along with the complete end of the affair of the Copts. Among the wonderful indications also is that if you look at the revelation of Bara'ah, you will find it was in the year nine of the Hijrah, during the Battle of Tabuk and after returning from it. So its being ninth and its descent in the ninth year indicates that the religion would become manifest over every opponent after nine years, which is the eighth year after the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), in the middle of the caliphate of al-Faruq (ʿUmar), when the Muslims prevailed over the Persians and the Romans, killed their men, and seized their wealth, just as it had become manifest at its descent over the idol-worshippers among the Arabs. Among the remarkable things is that the story of the Elephant occurred in the year of the birth of the Prophet (ﷺ), so it was forty years before the prophethood, corresponding to the number of words of the two surahs: al-Fil and Quraysh. The words of al-Fil are twenty-three and those of Quraysh are seventeen. This, and Allah knows best, is an indication that the beginning of security, through their destruction and the satisfaction of hunger by the plunder of what was with them of wealth and goods, was at the time of his birth (ﷺ) and the honouring of existence by his existence. This will be manifest, just as the cause, which is his existence (ﷺ), was manifest. It also indicates that his middle would be by his prophethood (ﷺ), and this will be inward, just as the cause, which is revelation, is inward. Then the security of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) occurred in the eighth year, corresponding to the number of words of the two basmalahs, through the hand of the Negus, king of Abyssinia, whose people had been the first to be destroyed for security to occur. If you add to these eleven pronouns, seven in al-Fil and four in Quraysh, they become fifty-nine, which correspond to the year six of the Hijrah if you count from the birth. In it occurred ʿUmrat al-Hudaybiyyah, which was the hidden, causal conquest (al-fath al-sababi al-khafi). To this the Prophet (ﷺ) pointed in his saying about the kneeling of his noble she-camel, when the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) said: "al-Qaswa has become restive," that is, she became stubborn:

«She has not become restive, but the one who restrained her is the one who restrained the Elephant.»

In it Surat al-Fath was revealed, so it was the cause of great security and wealth. After it, in the same year, came the sending of envoys to the kings of the regions, the conquest of Khaybar, and the spreading of the mention of Islam in all the lands. Likewise, after it and before ʿUmrat al-Qada', came the conversion of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs at the hand of the Negus, when he asked him to give him ʿAmr ibn Umayyah al-Damari (may Allah be pleased with him) so that he might kill him. That was when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to the Negus (may Allah be pleased with both of them) to invite him to Islam. The Negus rejected that from Ibn al-ʿAs and testified to the Prophet (ﷺ) that he was a Messenger, and ordered him to believe in him, so he did. Thus the king of Abyssinia, through the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ), became one who was saved and guided, and a caller to the Prophet (ﷺ), the opposite of what had been the case for the king of Abyssinia at his birth (ﷺ), namely that he was doomed, and headed toward the Blazing Fire. If you count from the year of the building of the Ka'bah, which was in the twenty-fifth year of his birth (ﷺ), the fifty-ninth year is the thirty-first after the Hijrah, which is the year of the eradication of the kingdom of the Persians through the killing of their last king, Yazdegerd. The Persians were those who removed the Abyssinians from the lands of Yemen and purified the land of the Arabs from them. Perhaps the division of the two surahs into twenty-three and seventeen is an indication that this noble birth, through which the Ka'bah was guarded and security and honour were attained by his blessing, would be renewed after some twenty years from his birth (ﷺ). They said: its building was when he was twenty-five years old, so it was probably at the end of his twenty-fourth year. Perhaps the story of the Elephant was when he was about one year old, and at the time of the building Allah brought together Quraysh after they had been extremely divided and had bound themselves to war over the matter of placing the Black Stone, [each claiming the right to place it] until Allah reconciled them through him (ﷺ). He placed it with his noble hand in a garment, and commanded them, so all the tribes took hold of its edges and lifted it until they reached its place, and then he (ﷺ) took it and placed it in its position. So the honour for reform and building was his alone. It also indicates that he would remain in prophethood for twenty-three years, after which Allah, glorified and exalted is He, would take him, after He had made the plots of all the disbelievers go astray, among the idol-worshippers, the Persians, the Romans and others, through what Allah opened for him of the Arabian Peninsula, by which Allah had united their word, until they flowed out over others, and no one agreed with them. They fought against him and contended with him in combat and wrestling. Perhaps the indication of Quraysh being seventeen words is that after seventeen years from the building of the House, He, glorified and exalted is He, would send him (ﷺ) to command Quraysh with worship, the most excellent of which is prayer, the greatest part of which is the obligatory prayers, which are seventeen rak'ahs, in gratitude for the blessing of the One who gave them security from fear and fed them after hunger, with the greatest of worship. It also indicates that the beginning of the union of Quraysh by a near power, close to action, after the great and manifest dispersion, and His making the plot of the disbelievers go astray, would occur in the seventeenth year of prophethood. That was the year four of the Hijrah, for in it occurred the expulsion of the Banu al-Nadir, Jews, from the noble city of Madinah, and Quraysh broke their promise in exchange for a promise, showing weakness in meeting the army of the Prophet (ﷺ). Shortly after that came the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said after they had withdrawn:

«Now we will attack them, and they will not attack us.»

He meant that the arrogance of Satan and the zeal of the Jahiliyyah among them had begun to fade, because their strength in falsehood, which had been the cause of their outward honour, had come to an end, and which was in reality their humiliation. That was the beginning of their inward honour, which is their humiliation before the people of Islam outwardly. After the Confederates came the Battle of the Banu Qurayzah. If you add to the words the four pronouns, they become twenty-one, which correspond to the year eight of the Hijrah. That was the year of the Greatest Conquest, by which the greatest union occurred among Quraysh, and their security and wealth, which Allah had promised them in the surah that corresponds to it, which is Bara'ah, through the union of all the Arabs and their rising, with their word gathered, to fight the Persians, the Romans and the Copts, and to take their lands, seize their treasures, and take control of their women and children. So glory be to Him whose speech this is, exalted is His rank and mighty is His purpose.
